fields.title: 2. Milestone E-2027-3 Verdict — Starting with the Definition
fields.md:
### 2-1. New Definition ① `definitions.conflict_intervention` (Conflict Intervention)

The September issue's milestone table states only "Zero recurrences of Starlink conflict intervention (Ukraine/Taiwan-type incidents) — Achieved: political risk contained / Missed: overseas government contract defections / Verification: media and government announcements" and does not define 'intervention' (source: `reports/2026-09.md`, Axis E table). Confirmed in this issue:

- **Conflict intervention** = an incident in which Starlink or Starshield service to a party to an armed conflict (or its military) was **restricted, blocked, or made conditional** by a **decision rather than a technical failure** (whether a company decision or the execution of a government order). The September 2022 non-activation incident near Crimea is the prototype (source: [Wikipedia — Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starlink_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war), for cross-checking ⑥).
- **Verification standard** = an official announcement by the government of the country concerned **AND** at least two top-tier news reports. Executive statements are used only for cross-checking (source: `prompts/monthly_run.md`, item 1, source priority ③·⑤).
- **The party giving the order is irrelevant to the verdict** — the milestone's meaning is "is Starlink perceived as a politically controllable service?", and that perception arises regardless of who gave the order (the risk of overseas government contract defections is the same).
- **Application to this incident**: government announcement (Ministry of Defense 10/24 · President 10/15~24) ✔ · top-tier reports (Reuters 10/15·23·24, WSJ 10/21) ✔ · non-technical decision ✔ → **1 conflict intervention** (source: Section 1).

### 2-2. New Definition ② `definitions.zero_event_milestone` (Verdict Timing for Zero-Event Milestones)

- The **measurement window** for the "zero recurrences" milestone is **cumulative from the baseline issue (2026-09-02) to the end of the verdict year (2027-12-31)**. The October issue counted "2026-09-02~10-23 no such incident found → 0," so it was already using a cumulative window (source: `state.milestones[E-2027-3].progress.source`, 2026-10-23).
- A cumulative zero target **cannot be reversed the moment one incident is confirmed** → it is marked **Missed** at the time of confirmation. This mirrors the fact that 'Achieved (early)' requires two consecutive quarters of fulfillment — early achievement can be reversed, so we wait; early miss cannot be reversed, so we do not wait (source: `definitions.early_achievement`, 2026-10-23).

### 2-3. Verdict

| Milestone | Previous (Issue 5) | This issue | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-2027-3 Zero recurrences of conflict intervention | 0 · In progress | **1 · Missed** | Section 1 facts ①~③ + 2-1 definition. progress.current = 1 (2026-10-13~24, Ukraine) |
| Axis E consecutive misses | 0 | **1** | The forced recalibration rule is 3 consecutive misses on the same axis — not triggered (source: `state.scorecard.forced_recalibration_rule`) |
| Scorecard | In progress 24 · Undetermined 5 · Missed 0 | **In progress 23 · Undetermined 5 · Missed 1** | Formula: 24 − 1 = 23 |

(source: `state.milestones` · `state.scorecard`, 2026-10-27)

**Adjacent milestones not touched (reasons)**: For E-2027-4 (new U.S. federal contract wins ≥ prior year), there are calls for a congressional inquiry, but the contract-win figures have not changed — remains undetermined. A-2030-1 (licenses in the top 10 overseas markets) and E-2028-1 (licenses maintained in 5 countries) will be touched **when an "overseas government contract defection" is confirmed by official announcement** — this issue's search found no official announcement of termination or replacement procurement (reports of a rebound in European satellite stocks are a price reaction, not a contract event) (source: [roic.ai 10/14 search summary](https://www.roic.ai/news/spacex-restricts-starlink-for-ukrainian-military-disrupting-drone-missions-10-14-2026) · Section 1).
